methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vn -c:a mp2 -b:a 192k soundtrack.mp2.
methods.limits: -vn disables video; the MP2 encoder is in FFmpeg's audio codec list.

methods.steps: With the optional FFmpeg library installed, import the MP4 audio; File > Export Audio; select MP2 in the Format list.
methods.limits: Import of MP4 needs the optional FFmpeg library; MP2 bit rate 16 to 384 kbps, default 160.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vn -c:a pcm_s16le extracted.wav, then twolame -b 192 extracted.wav soundtrack.mp2.
methods.limits: Two-stage method; TwoLAME reads input through libsndfile and -b sets the total bitrate in kbps.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -c:a mp2 -c:v mpeg2video converted.mpg.
methods.limits: Set destination-required parameters explicitly; the documentation lists MP2 audio and MPEG-2 video among supported codecs.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -target pal-dvd dvd-ready.mpg; the target type may be prefixed with pal-, ntsc- or film-.
methods.limits: Encoded media is not an authored DVD.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i clip.mpeg animation.gif.
methods.limits: The GIF muxer loops indefinitely by default and cannot make the delay between frames smaller than one centisecond.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -t 5 -i clip.mpeg short.gif.
methods.limits: -t before -i limits the duration of data read from the input.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i clip.mpeg -vf palettegen colors.png, then ffmpeg -i clip.mpeg -i colors.png -lavfi paletteuse animation.gif.
methods.limits: palettegen generates one palette for the whole video; paletteuse uses it to downsample the stream.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i archive.mpg -c:a aac -c:v libx264 viewing.mov.
methods.limits: Fresh lossy encoding; select parameters required by the receiver.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i archive.mpg -c copy repacked.mov.
methods.limits: Only compatible streams can be muxed; the receiving application must decode them.

methods.steps: Select pictures; click Export; choose JPEG, choose where to save, then Export.
methods.limits: Verify raw variant support and development choices.

methods.steps: Select a supported raw image; in export choose file on disk and JPEG, choose a location, then export.
methods.limits: Nikon high-efficiency NEFs are explicitly unsupported.

methods.steps: Run magick source.nef sharing.jpeg.
methods.limits: The formats page lists NEF as readable and JPEG as readable and writable.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i source.ogv -c:a aac -c:v libx264 ogv-delivery.mp4.
methods.limits: Re-encodes rather than copying Ogg streams.

methods.steps: Media > Convert/Save; add OGV, set a destination file and a Profile; Start.
methods.limits: The documented walkthrough does not list profile names; Ogg and Theora input are listed on the features page.

methods.steps: Run opusdec message.opus decoded.wav.
methods.limits: opusdec writes WAVE output when the output filename ends in .wav.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i message.opus -c:a pcm_s16le editable.wav.
methods.limits: -vn removes video; the source encode's discarded detail is not restored.

methods.steps: Run pnmtopng render.ppm > render.png.
methods.limits: Netpbm documents automatic maxval scaling to 255 or 65535.

methods.steps: Run magick render.ppm delivered.png.
methods.limits: The formats page lists PPM and PNG as readable and writable.

methods.steps: Open PPM; File > Export As; export as PNG.
methods.limits: The export page gives the menu path; file-pnm.c shows PPM loading.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i legacy.qt -c:a aac -c:v libx264 quicktime-delivery.mp4.
methods.limits: Re-encodes; source codecs must first be decodable.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i legacy.qt -c copy quicktime-remux.mp4.
methods.limits: Works only with streams the MP4 muxer can carry.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -t 10 -i legacy.qt -c:a aac -c:v libx264 first-ten.mp4.
methods.limits: -t before -i limits the duration of data read from the input.

methods.steps: Add WMV to a project; click Export; choose GIF.
methods.limits: GIF is offered for videos of 15 seconds or less.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -t 4 -i training.wmv excerpt.gif.
methods.limits: -t before -i limits how much of the input is read.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i training.wmv -vf palettegen wmv-colors.png, then ffmpeg -i training.wmv -i wmv-colors.png -lavfi paletteuse wmv-animation.gif.
methods.limits: Keep any trim and scale settings consistent across passes.
